newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta sees seven hour frost, Prairies wet, cool.
newsitem.headline: Alberta sees seven hour frost, Prairies wet, cool.

text.p: South and central Alberta saw temperatures drop below freezing at midnight and stay there past 0730 CDT/1230 GMT Tuesday, Environment Canada said.
Lethbridge, in southeast Alberta, was at -3.0 Celsius since midnight, meteorologist Mike Russo said.
Alberta Wheat Pool on Friday said Lethbridge district was 96 percent harvested.
Edson, west of Edmonton, was at or below -2.0 Celsius since midnight.
Central Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete, Alberta Agriculture said.
Calgary recorded a low of 0 Celsius (32 F).
"Elsewhere in Saskatchewan and western Manitoba there was too much cloud cover for things to go below zero," Russo said.
Val Marie, in southwest Saskatchewan above the Montana border, saw five hours below freezing. Estevan, in southeast Saskatchewan above the North Dakota border, was at 0 Celsius at 0700 CDT/1200 GMT.
Saskatchewan's southern grainbelt harvested 61 percent of all crops, Saskatchewan Agriculture said.
Sprague, in southeast Manitoba above the Minnesota border, was at or below -1.0 Celsius from 0300 to 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
Alberta should see rain in the east and northeast with highs of nine and 13 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see a few showers with highs of 10 Celsius.
Manitoba should see scattered showers and highs of 14 Celsius.
